title: Janis at the Store
c1_label: Buy flour and hear the safer road
c1_result: Janis chalks a line on the counter. 'The road holds above this mark. Below it, nothing holds.'
c2_label: Ask what the valley asks of travelers
c2_result: He thinks before answering. 'Ask before you take. Pay what a thing is worth, not what it costs you.'
c3_result: Janis counts it twice and doesn't look up. A fair sale, nothing more.

title: A Map With Blanks
c1_label: Give him the names Janis taught you
c1_result: Ames writes quickly and thanks you twice. Whatever you said is now what the map says.
c2_label: Ask whose names he means to write
c2_result: Ames pauses. 'The army's, I suppose.' Then, quietly: 'Is that wrong?'
c3_result: The white on his map stays white. For now.

title: Little Willow at the Ford
c1_label: Hire her to guide the ford (-1 trade goods)
c1_result: She walks you across by a line you would never have chosen. The wagon barely wets its axle.
c2_label: Share your food and ask about the old trails
c2_result: She tells you the high route the Ute families use in summer, and the crossing the Arapaho prefer in spring. You cannot write it down fast enough.
c3_result: You find the ford the hard way. The horses remember it better than you do.

title: Chief Friday's Counsel
c1_label: Listen and slow your pace
c1_result: You leave with sharper eyes. The valley feels less like scenery and more like obligation.
c2_result: Respect offered carefully and received in kind. He asks after Janis, and you answer more honestly than you meant to.
c3_label: Press on with the stage timetable
c3_result: You keep the company clock. It is not the only clock in this country.

title: What the River Remembers
c1_label: Ask for the names, and promise to carry them accurately
c1_result: He gives them slowly and corrects you without unkindness. You write nothing down. You will have to remember.
c2_label: Ask where the high water will come
c2_result: He points at the bend, then at the sky, then at your wagon. 'Not tonight. Soon.'
c3_result: He nods. The leaving is respected, and remembered.

title: Virginia at the Home Station
c1_label: Offer to help with the horses
c1_result: She hands you a currycomb without a word. By dusk the station remembers useful hands.
c2_result: Her look tells you the question was cheaper than the answer. 'Ask the river,' she says. 'It knew him longer.'
c3_label: Offer to carry her letter east
c3_result: She writes for a long time, seals it, and presses it into your hand. It weighs more than paper.

title: Older Than the River's Name
c1_label: Keep it
c1_result: It is warm from the sun and heavier than it looks. You wrap it in a rag and tell yourself it is only a curiosity.
c2_result: You set it back in the gravel, edge up, where the next rain will find it. Something in your chest unclenches.
c3_result: Virginia turns it in the light. 'Jack would have sold it by supper,' she says, and hands it back with both hands.

title: Mason Makes His Choice
c1_label: Trade with him anyway
c1_result: You gain provisions by stepping closer to the new order. It pays promptly, and it will remember.
c2_result: You leave poorer in goods and clearer in mind.
c3_label: Ask what the claim is for
c3_result: 'Order,' he says. 'A place where a person cannot be mistaken for someone else's trespass.' He believes it.

title: A Collector's Offer
c1_label: Sell it to him
c1_result: The goods are real, and so is a weight you did not expect. A made thing has left the river for good.
c2_result: 'Sentiment,' he says, and shrugs. You keep it. Whether that is better is a harder question.

title: A Paper to Witness
c1_label: Sign as witness
c1_result: The ink is dry before you finish being sorry. The word 'vacant' will outlast the argument.
c2_result: Mason listens to every word. 'Then it is a fact you chose not to attest to,' he says. 'I will remember.'
c3_label: Ask who lives on the land it describes
c3_result: He does not answer. The silence is the answer, and the paper stays unsigned.

title: High Water
c1_label: Save your wagon and flour
c1_result: You lose a day's gear to the current but keep the wagon and what is in it. Others watch you do it.
c2_label: Help pull people from the bank
c2_result: Your hands are raw by morning. A woman whose name you never learn presses a pouch of dried meat into them.
c3_label: Climb for high ground and wait it out
c3_result: You are dry and ashamed in about equal measure. The river takes what it takes.

title: Names on the Map
c1_label: Give every name, and say where you learned it
c1_result: He writes, then underlines. 'I'll credit them,' he says, 'as far as the margin allows.'
c2_label: Give only a few, to be safe
c2_result: Some names fit on the paper. Most are still only in you.
c3_label: Say nothing. They are not yours to give
c3_result: The blank stays blank. Whether that protects the names or erases them, you will not know for years.

title: Mason's Line
c1_label: Let it stand
c1_result: It is clear. It is also wrong in ways the map has no way to say.
c2_label: Ask Ames to redraw the river as it really runs
c2_result: Ames redraws the bend by hand. It is a small correction, and it is the one that will matter in spring.
c3_result: The line stays. So does your silence.

title: The Survey
c1_label: Tell him what you saw, plainly
c1_result: He writes it down, correct and incomplete. Most maps are.
c2_result: He nods and looks back at the paper. The blanks are still blanks.

title: Hail on the Prairie
c1_label: Shelter under the wagon and wait
c1_result: You wait it out with the team trembling. Nothing breaks but your schedule.
c2_result: You make the trees. The horses very nearly don't.

title: A Rising Ford
c1_label: Wait a day for it to drop
c1_result: By morning the water has dropped a hand's breadth. Patience, as usual, is cheaper than a wagon.
c2_result: You cross, but the dry-goods barrel doesn't. It could have been worse.
c3_label: Pay the freighter to pull you through (-1 trade goods)
c3_result: He charges for the rope and the lecture.

title: The Stage Goes By
c1_label: Read the paper
c1_result: Column after column about the war and the price of flour. Nothing about this valley, which says something.
c2_result: It burns badly and smells of ink.

title: Pronghorn on the Rise
c1_label: Hunt (-3 ammo)
c1_result: One clean shot. You carry meat into camp and nobody argues about supper.
c2_result: They watch you go. It feels a little like being forgiven.

title: Fever in the Wagon
c1_label: Use a dose of medicine (-1 medicine)
c1_result: By morning the fever breaks. You count the bottle again.
c2_label: Sit it out and trust rest
c2_result: The fever breaks late and takes a day from everyone.

title: Arapaho Family on the Road
c1_label: Trade for dried meat (-1 trade goods)
c1_result: A fair trade, fairly made. They do not ask where you are going.
c2_result: They tell you the river is rising upstream. They do not say it as advice.

title: A Patrol Wants Names
c1_label: Answer everything
c1_result: He writes it all down. A mile on you realize you have just drawn a map for someone.
c2_label: Tell him what you saw, not who
c2_result: He sighs and lets you pass.
c3_result: He knows you are lying. You know he knows. Neither of you says so.
